DESIGN THESIS
Every campaign battle is a bespoke, legal, readable puzzle. The player receives competitive Pokemon, moves, abilities, natures, Stat Points, and free ordinary held items; difficulty comes from decisions rather than grinding.
Hard is authored. Medium subtracts two opposing levels. Easy subtracts four. Teams and AI stay identical.
Mega Evolution is the only selectable gimmick. No Mega appears before the post-Brawly bracelet. Primals remain approved automatic forms.
Bosses are difficulty 10. Ordinary trainers deliberately vary in simultaneous demands so the campaign remains difficult without becoming exhausting.

REMATCH POLICY
Ordinary and Gym rematches are not campaign content. League replays reuse the finished League teams. Gabby and Ty remain only as distinct roaming reporter milestones. Repeatable endgame variety belongs to the live Champions Circuit reached from every Frontier challenge desk.

IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT
Implement every retained branch exactly: format, cap-relative levels, species, item, ability, nature, Stat Points, moves, AI requirements, and native dialogue intent. Compile after each 100 implemented encounters, then run source, static, emulator, save, and full-progression gates.

primary_question: Can the chosen starter beat its same-generation type counter when neither side has a captured team yet?
theme_and_tempo: The rival's species is resolved from the player's starter generation and choice. Every branch is level 13 with a Life Orb, perfect preparation, its legal Pledge STAB, Protect, and two species-specific current moves: Treecko and Torchic can threaten setup while Mudkip commits to immediate physical pressure.
intentional_weakness: This is a one-on-one with no hidden reserve. Focus Sash, Eviolite, Leftovers, priority, status, setup denial, Counter or Mirror Coat, Endeavor, recovery, and direct coverage all provide different solutions across the starter families.

strongest_part: The same rule produces a fair but different opening puzzle for every starter family without pretending all starters want the same four moves.
weakest_link: A one-Pokemon fight cannot create switching depth; its value is the immediate lesson that held items and authored sets matter from battle one.

primary_question: Can the player identify the false ace, manage its support, and preserve an answer for the real Mew?
theme_and_tempo: Zorua leads beside Friend Guard Jigglypuff while Illusion makes it appear to be the Mew held in the final slot. Icy Wind and Helping Hand turn the false Mew into immediate pressure; Focus Sash Smeargle then creates a redirection or Fake Out window for the real Mew to use Nasty Plot and clean.
intentional_weakness: This team has several answers rather than one key. Spread attacks expose Illusion and bypass Follow Me, Taunt shuts down Jigglypuff or Smeargle, priority finishes a Sash-broken Smeargle, and early Bug, Ghost, and Dark options pressure Mew. The player can also double-target the support slot, contest speed with their own Icy Wind or Electroweb, or overwhelm the frail Zorua lead.
first_loss_lesson: Break Illusion early and remove the support slot before spending the team's best Dark, Bug, or Ghost answer.
strongest_part: Zorua's Dark Pulse creates a readable handoff through Jigglypuff, Smeargle into Mew's Nasty Plot, so the team has one identity without becoming one scripted solution.
weakest_link: If the player breaks the redirection layer or removes Zorua early, the remaining members must win through ordinary positioning; that intentional seam keeps difficulty 7.6 honest.

physical_group_id: BATTLE_007_ROUTE_104_DARIAN
proposed_encounter_id: BATTLE_007_ROUTE_104_DARIAN
campaign_order: 7
atlas_ordinal: 7

location: Route104
requirement: optional talk
status: master_audited_ready_for_implementation
quality_target: 10
difficulty_target: 7.8
difficulty_observed: UNPLAYED
fatigue_role: ordinary_standard
primary_question: Can the player weaken the first cast's Water Spout while keeping enough denial for the second cast's Shell Smash?
theme_and_tempo: Cap-relative Choice Scarf Remoraid and Expert Belt Dazzling Bruxish form the first cast: full-HP Water Spout attacks immediately while Dazzling blocks priority and Bruxish applies Taunt, screen breaking, and physical coverage. Sitrus Intimidate Qwilfish and cap-relative Focus Sash Clamperl form the second cast: Thunder Wave and Intimidate buy one Shell Smash opportunity, then Muddy Water or Ice Beam converts it into pressure.
